title: Generation of neutron Bessel beams
byline: Lailey; Owen; Sarenac; Dusan; Emelianenko; Nir; Clark; Charles W; Cory; David G; Ekinci; Huseyin; Huber; Michael G; Paster; Jeremy W; Sokolova; Anna; Venero; Di
html:
Abstract:Matter waves can exhibit structured wavefields analogous to those of light, offering new means of controlling the spatial and angular-momentum degrees of freedom of massive particles. Bessel beams are a fundamental class of structured waves that exhibit non-diffracting propagation, self-healing, and well-defined orbital angular momentum (OAM). Here, we experimentally realize neutron Bessel beams by imprinting a nanoscale conical phase gradient onto a neutron wavefront. By incorporating azimuthal phase gradients, we generate zeroth-, third-, and sixth-order Bessel beams, demonstrating direct control of both the OAM and radial structure of a massive particle. We also propose a neutron Bessel-grating interferometer, complementary to established optical and electron interferometric methods, in which varying the radial grating period by approximately 100 nm yields a controlled Gouy phase shift of $\pi$. These results establish neutron Bessel beams as a new platform for diffractive neutron focusing and provide an experimental foundation for theoretical studies of Bessel beams in neutron scattering, decay, and OAM characterization.
